ideas.label: Fortress
ideas.principle: Test the defender's setup for zugzwang or a second weakness before assuming it c
ideas.summary: A material advantage does not guarantee a win when the defender can build a fortress. Before simplifying, identify whether the defending king and pieces can hold fixed squares without being forced to concede.

ideas.label: Fortress
ideas.principle: Stretch an opposite-bishop fortress across two fronts.
ideas.summary: Opposite-colored bishop endings often become fortresses because the defender can control the promotion color while the attacking bishop cannot challenge it. Keep pawns on squares the defending bishop must guard and seek threats on both wings.

ideas.label: Fortress
ideas.principle: Recognize the wrong-bishop rook-pawn fortress before trading into it.
ideas.summary: Against a bishop-and-rook-pawn fortress, first verify whether the bishop controls the pawn's promotion square. If the defending king can reach the corner that the bishop cannot drive it from, the extra pawn may be useless.
